en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands, with only about 2,000 of them permanently inhabited.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features an 8.2-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of approximately 911 square kilometers.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers to the Pacific Ocean.
The Philippine tarsier is one of the smallest primates, measuring only 85 to 160 millimeters in total body length.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into mountains over 2,000 years ago and reach elevations up to 1,500 meters.
The Philippine Trench reaches a maximum depth of 10,540 meters, making it one of the deepest oceanic trenches.
The Philippines currently has exactly 24 active volcanoes monitored by scientists, including Mayon, Taal, and Kanlaon.
Rafflesia schadenbergiana, a rare plant in Mount Apo, produces the largest flowers in the Philippines, measuring up to 80 centimeters wide.
Palawan is the longest province in the country, stretching approximately 425 kilometers between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
Mayon Volcano has a perfect cone shape and has erupted over 50 times in the last 400 years.
